text.paragraph: Alert and engaged. Independent in all activities; working full time but exhausted in the mornings after evenings of bingeing and vomiting. Examination: lying blood pressure 102/64 and pulse 66; after three minutes standing 98/62 and pulse 88, a rise of 22 per minute, without dizziness; both parotid glands visibly enlarged and non-tender; enamel erosion on the inner surfaces of the upper front teeth; small calluses on the backs of two knuckles of the right hand; no edema; skin intact, no scars of recent self-injury. [S]

Vital signs recorded on 2026-02-09; see the Vital Signs section. Mental status: Alert, articulate, and warm; tearful and ashamed when describing the bingeing and vomiting, and relieved to have said it; thought process organized; no psychotic features; insight good; Mood low, tired, and hopeless about stopping; feels worthless; PHQ-9 14 with item 9 scored 0; no current thoughts of suicide or self-harm. The physical examination is limited to the findings relevant to this synthetic episode. [S]

Structured safety assessment: current ideation absent, intent absent, plan absent, access to means reviewed: yes. Outpatient care with close follow-up. She has no current thoughts of suicide or self-harm and no self-injury now; past self-injury at a time of great distress is part of her history and was discussed with her gently. Eating disorders and depression both raise the risk of suicide and self-harm, so a written safety plan was made with her, with her own warning signs (a run of bad nights of bingeing, feeling hopeless, or wanting to hurt herself) and what to do about each, including whom to call. Lethal-means counseling: no firearm and no access to one; medicines are kept in small amounts. The 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline (call or text 988) was given and saved in her phone, with the clinic number. Safety reviewed at every visit. [S]

tr.td: Bulimia nervosa, severe: recurrent binge eating, each time with self-induced vomiting, averaging about ten episodes a week for about three years, hidden from everyone; self-worth tied closely to body shape and weight; no laxatives, diuretics, diet pills, or excessive exercise. SCOFF 4 of 5; EDE-Q global score 3.9. Findings: bilateral parotid enlargement, enamel erosion on the inner surfaces of the upper front teeth, calluses on the backs of two knuckles of the right hand, a pulse rise of 22 per minute on standing, low potassium and chloride with a raised bicarbonate, and a raised amylase; BMI 19.3. Synthetic modern episode linked to her own public account of bulimia
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis by DSM-5-TR criteria; severity is graded by the average number of compensatory episodes a week (8 to 13 is severe).
Hypokalemia (potassium 3.1 mmol/L) with low chloride and metabolic alkalosis from repeated vomiting; QTc 452 ms; no palpitations, weakness, or fainting
S — Synthetic presenting laboratory finding; resolved when potassium was normal on two checks.

Medical risk assessment and monitoring for purging: orthostatic vital signs and weight at every visit, potassium, chloride, bicarbonate and creatinine weekly until potassium is normal twice and then at each visit, magnesium and phosphate at baseline and when potassium is low, an ECG at baseline and after any QT-relevant medicine change while potassium is low, and urgent or inpatient care for potassium below 3.0 mmol/L despite replacement, QTc above 500 ms, fainting, a pulse below 50, or blood in the vomit. Guideline: The American Psychiatric Association Practice Guideline for the Treatment of Patients With Eating Disorders, Fourth Edition (2023); Eating disorders: recognition and treatment (NICE guideline NG69) (2017, updated 2020) [S]

Eating disorders psychiatry consultation on the diagnosis and its severity, the right level of care, psychological treatment, fluoxetine, and medical monitoring. Guideline: The American Psychiatric Association Practice Guideline for the Treatment of Patients With Eating Disorders, Fourth Edition (2023); Eating disorders: recognition and treatment (NICE guideline NG69) (2017, updated 2020) [S]

Oral potassium chloride 20 mEq twice daily, with a recheck in one week; stopped once potassium is normal and vomiting is less frequent. Guideline: The American Psychiatric Association Practice Guideline for the Treatment of Patients With Eating Disorders, Fourth Edition (2023); Eating disorders: recognition and treatment (NICE guideline NG69) (2017, updated 2020) [S]

Nutrition: an eating disorders dietitian; regular eating of three meals and two or three snacks a day, no dieting or skipped meals, and no foods banned; caffeine cut down. Guideline: The American Psychiatric Association Practice Guideline for the Treatment of Patients With Eating Disorders, Fourth Edition (2023); Eating disorders: recognition and treatment (NICE guideline NG69) (2017, updated 2020) [S]

Dental protection while vomiting continues: no brushing for an hour after vomiting, a non-acid fluoride mouthwash, fewer acidic drinks, and a dental examination. Guideline: Eating disorders: recognition and treatment (NICE guideline NG69) (2017, updated 2020) [S]

Structured safety assessment, a written safety plan with her warning signs, lethal-means counseling, the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline, the PHQ-9 at each visit, and safety review at every visit.
